summary: Dependency-confusion package sends host and install details to a remote server at install time
details: @drone-js-ext/vip-badge is a dependency-confusion package: it squats the `@drone-js-ext` scope, which matches a private internal package scope, and was published on 2026-10-25 in versions 0.0.1, 1.0.1, 2.0.0, 99.0.1 (up to 99.0.1) so that builds resolving the internal name from the public registry install it instead. Its `postinstall` script runs `node beacon.cjs`, which sends an HTTP POST over cleartext HTTP to the hardcoded IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` with the package name, the machine's hostname, the install directory, the current working directory and the Node.js version, tagged with an `x-beacon-package` header. The entry point `index.js` sends the same request again whenever the package is loaded and otherwise exports a Proxy whose every property is a no-op function, so it has no legitimate functionality and hides the missing API from bundlers. The README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test"; that does not change what it does to an installer. The same beacon code and endpoint appear in other dependency-confusion packages from the same publisher. The inert `0.0.0-stage` and `0.1.0` placeholder versions carry no install script and are not affected. Any machine that installed an affected version has disclosed its hostname and filesystem layout to a third party; remove the package, pin or scope internal package names to the internal registry, and block 185.158.107.175 on build hosts.
